proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay and fractional effects can be confounded with transmission/waning, yielding unstable timing or overly sharp peaks when extrapolating beyond the observed season.
proposals.rationale: Matches prior discovered pattern and aligns with hospitalization-rate semantics where admissions plausibly lag the infectious proxy; SEIRS supports sharp seasonal peaks via waning immunity while fractional dynamics can flexibly capture high peakiness with limited training length.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admission lag is closer to 2–3 weeks, forecasts may peak too early and underrepresent the right-tail decline.
proposals.rationale: A more parsimonious lag than 2 weeks to hedge against over-shifting peak timing; retains SEIRS+fractional flexibility for high peakiness while respecting recommended delayed observation semantics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a single short season, leading to parameter tradeoffs (I→H vs recovery) and unstable amplitude forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the target to an explicit hospitalization compartment, consistent with surveillance semantics; kept non-fractional to reduce degrees of freedom given short series and identifiability concerns.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May blur mechanistic interpretation and overestimate baseline levels by attributing too much signal to I, degrading peak height calibration for hospitalization-rate targets.
proposals.rationale: Uses combined burden (infectious plus hospitalized) as an observation proxy to reduce sensitivity to how cases split between I and H, potentially stabilizing fits when H alone is noisy or weakly identified.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Without waning immunity, may misrepresent post-peak dynamics (too slow/fast decline) and struggle if the series reflects within-season susceptibility replenishment effects.
proposals.rationale: More parsimonious than SEIRS while still allowing a lagged infectious proxy for admissions; fractional dynamics can accommodate high peakiness without adding waning-immunity parameters.
